description: Add a monster reset feature (GitHub issue #20). Returns the current monster to its initial state (a fresh baby egg: trainingCount, stats, careCounters, hunger, elapsed time all reset), guarded by a confirm step to prevent accidental resets, with JA/EN UI text. DESIGN DECISION (document in the handback report): reset keeps the SAME browser monsterId and OVERWRITES the existing DynamoDB record with a fresh baby via the existing POST /monster endpoint. This is the simplest approach that stays consistent with the no-auth, browser-owned-id design: the backend upserts by monsterId (single record), localStorage 'ddm.monsterId' is unchanged, and no new backend/infra endpoint is needed (frontend-only change -> no backend redeploy required beyond the normal frontend redeploy the orchestrator performs). The reset uses the same default hatch name 'でじたん' that useMonster uses on first hatch (keeps hatch and reset consistent).
steps: In packages/frontend/src/state/useMonster.ts add a `reset: () => Promise<void>` to the UseMonsterState interface and implement it in the hook. Model it on the existing care-action pattern (runCareAction): guard early-return when monster is null OR busy; setBusy(true); setError(null). Build a fresh baby with `createMonster(current.id, DEFAULT_MONSTER_NAME, Date.now())` where DEFAULT_MONSTER_NAME is 'でじたん' (reuse the same literal the mount hatch uses — extract it to a named const used by BOTH the mount hatch and reset so they can never drift).

On reset, prevent a spurious evolution banner: because commit() fires setJustEvolvedTo when prevStageRef.current !== next.stageId, resetting from e.g. ultimate to baby would wrongly trigger the banner. Set prevStageRef.current = fresh.stageId BEFORE calling commit(fresh) (or clear it to null then set it) so the baby reset never fires the 'evolved!' banner. Also call setJustEvolvedTo(null) to dismiss any banner currently showing.
On reset, clear transient UI state that belonged to the old monster: setBattleLog([]), setLastBattle(null), setChatLog([]). Leave busy/error handling to the standard pattern.

Persist the reset: await api.saveMonster(fresh) and commit the returned monster (same optimistic -> commit(fresh) -> try save -> commit(saved) -> catch setError -> finally setBusy(false) shape as runCareAction). If the save fails, keep the optimistic fresh baby locally and surface the error (matching care-action behavior).
Export `reset` from the hook's returned object.

In packages/frontend/src/i18n.ts add new keys to BOTH JA_MESSAGES and EN_MESSAGES (required or tsc fails): 'reset.button' (e.g. JA 'リセット', EN 'Reset'), 'reset.confirmTitle' or 'reset.confirmPrompt' (JA e.g. 'モンスターを初期状態（新しい卵）に戻します。トレーニング回数・ステータス・経過はすべてリセットされます。よろしいですか？', EN equivalent), 'reset.confirm' (JA 'リセットする', EN 'Reset'), and 'reset.cancel' (JA 'キャンセル', EN 'Cancel'). Keep JA output for all EXISTING keys byte-identical; only ADD keys.

In packages/frontend/src/App.tsx wire `game.reset` and add a small, visually-distinct reset control with a confirm step so a single accidental click cannot wipe progress. Implement the confirm as a two-step inline control OR a small confirm panel/dialog (no new dependency; use local useState like the existing careFx state): first click shows the confirm prompt (t('reset.confirmPrompt')) with Confirm (t('reset.confirm')) and Cancel (t('reset.cancel')) buttons; Confirm calls game.reset() and hides the prompt, Cancel just hides it. Disable the control while game.busy or game.loading or game.monster===null. Place it sensibly (e.g. in the header near the lang toggle, or in the controls-area near the stats). Use t('reset.button') for the trigger label.

In packages/frontend/src/styles.css add styles for the reset button and the confirm prompt (make the reset button visually distinct, e.g. a muted/danger accent, and the confirm prompt clearly readable). Follow existing button styling conventions (see .care-btn / .lang-btn).

OPTIONAL but preferred: if any pure/testable logic is introduced (e.g. a helper returning the default reset name/state), add it to packages/frontend/src/ui-helpers.ts and unit-test it in packages/frontend/src/game-ui.test.ts following the existing test style. If reset is a thin wrapper over createMonster (already covered by shared tests), a dedicated unit test may not be needed; in that case document the manual/Playwright verification instead. Do NOT add a trivial test that only asserts a constant.
acceptance_criteria: useMonster exposes reset(); calling it replaces the current monster with a fresh baby (stageId 'baby', trainingCount 0, careCounters zeroed, hungryLevel 0, dirty false, baby baseStats) under the SAME monster id, and persists it via api.saveMonster.
After reset, no evolution banner is shown (prevStageRef is reset so baby does not fire a spurious 'evolved!'), and battleLog/lastBattle/chatLog are cleared.
The reset trigger requires a confirm step (two-step button or confirm prompt) before the monster is reset; Cancel aborts with no state change.
The reset control is disabled while busy/loading/no-monster.
New i18n keys exist in BOTH ja and en dictionaries; JA output for all existing keys is unchanged.
`npm run build` (root) succeeds (this proves i18n key parity and types).
Root `npm test` and `cd packages/frontend && npm test` still pass (no regression); any new unit test passes.
verification: npm run build (root) exits 0 with no TS errors
cd packages/frontend && npm test all pass

Manual/Playwright (optional, local build on a dev server): train/feed to change stats, click Reset, confirm, and observe the monster returns to a fresh baby with trainingCount 0 and no evolution banner
findings: Implemented frontend-only reset keeping the same browser monsterId and overwriting the single DynamoDB record via the existing POST /monster (api.saveMonster). No backend/infra change. Files changed: packages/frontend/src/state/useMonster.ts, packages/frontend/src/i18n.ts, packages/frontend/src/App.tsx, packages/frontend/src/styles.css. useMonster: added exported shared const DEFAULT_MONSTER_NAME = 'でじたん' (reused by BOTH the mount hatch and reset so they can't drift), added reset:()=>Promise<void> to UseMonsterState and implemented it on the runCareAction pattern (guard monster===null||busy; setBusy(true); setError(null); fresh=createMonster(current.id, DEFAULT_MONSTER_NAME, Date.now()); set prevStageRef.current=fresh.stageId and setJustEvolvedTo(null) BEFORE commit to avoid a spurious evolution banner; clear setBattleLog([])/setLastBattle(null)/setChatLog([]); commit(fresh); await api.saveMonster(fresh)->commit(saved); catch->setError; finally setBusy(false)); exported reset. New i18n keys (ja/en): reset.button 'リセット'/'Reset'; reset.confirmPrompt 'モンスターを初期状態（新しい卵）に戻します。トレーニング回数・ステータス・経過はすべてリセットされます。よろしいですか？'/'This returns your monster to its initial state (a fresh egg). Training count, stats, and progress will all be reset. Are you sure?'; reset.confirm 'リセットする'/'Reset'; reset.cancel 'キャンセル'/'Cancel'. All existing JA keys left byte-identical (only added). Reset control lives in the app header inside a new .header-controls wrapper to the left of the language toggle; it is disabled while game.busy||game.loading||game.monster===null. Confirm UX: first click sets local confirmingReset state (useState, mirroring careFx) which renders a .reset-confirm alertdialog panel below the header with the prompt plus Confirm (calls game.reset() then hides) and Cancel (just hides) buttons. styles.css: added .header-controls, .reset-btn (danger-accent, muted/disabled state, .confirm variant), .reset-confirm panel, .reset-confirm-text, .reset-confirm-actions, .reset-cancel-btn following .lang-btn/.care-btn conventions. No dedicated unit test added: reset is a thin wrapper over shared createMonster (already covered by shared's 47 tests) and the briefing says not to add a trivial constant-only test; verification is the typecheck (build) + manual/Playwright. Verification run and GREEN: root `npm run build` exit 0 (proves TS types + i18n ja/en key parity); root `npm test` 47 pass / 0 fail; `cd packages/frontend && npm test` 50 pass / 0 fail. Manual/Playwright note: on a local dev server, train/feed to change stats, click Reset, click リセットする/Reset in the confirm panel, and confirm the monster returns to a fresh baby (stageId 'baby', trainingCount 0) with no evolution banner and cleared battle/chat logs; Cancel aborts with no state change.
